question.text: Active fixed-income managers track three aspects of the yield curve — the '3S'. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

explanation.text: The Logic: The three S's of the yield curve are Shift, Slope and Shape, with shape decided by the curvature / convexity of the curve. Sector is not one of the three. The Trap: Sector matters for credit and cross-sectional bond selection, but it is not part of the yield-curve-movement framework that the 3S describe. Note: Shift captures parallel up/down moves; slope captures steepening/flattening; shape captures curvature changes.
